# Seeing and changing print settings

Where the settings of a print are shown in JusPrin, and the ways to change them.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are inside the menu at the left of the title bar.

<!-- ai: This guide is the by-hand route. When the person wants a setting changed and has not said they want to do it themselves, I change it with my settings tools. I give these steps when they ask where something is or want to do it themselves. -->

## See the settings a print will use

The **Setup summary** card at the top of the AI panel names the process and filament presets in use and says how many settings differ from them. If the AI panel is hidden, open the **View** menu and choose **Show AI panel** (on Windows and Linux, tick **AI panel**).

![The Setup summary card at the top of the AI panel, with the All settings link at its right](pictures/print-settings/setup-summary.png)

To see every setting:

1. On the Setup summary card, click **All settings**. The link is there once AI is set up.
2. Under **Showing**, pick **Whole project**, one plate, or one object. Plates are listed when the project has two or more. The list also follows what is selected in the 3D view.
3. Type in **Search settings** to find a setting by name, or switch from **All** to **Changed** to see only the settings that differ from the presets.
4. Click **Back to chat** to close the list.

![The All settings list, showing the whole project, with the Search settings box and the All and Changed switch](pictures/print-settings/all-settings.png)

The settings are grouped as Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial and Others, then Filament and Printer. The list is for reading: a value cannot be typed into it.

## Change a print setting

Print settings are things like layer height, infill, supports and speed. JusPrin's own view has no field to type them into. There are two ways to change one:

- Ask AI in the chat, for example "set the layer height to 0.16 mm". The change is then listed in the chat with the old and the new value.
- Switch to classic view, which has every print setting on screen. See [Classic view](#classic-view-every-setting-on-screen).

## Take a settings change back

- Each change made in a chat is listed in that chat. Point at a change and click the curved-arrow button at its right, named **Revert to here**. Then click **Revert to here** in the question that opens. The model and the project's settings go back to that point. The current model is saved in Version history first, and the chat, exported files and finished prints stay as they are.

![The Revert to here question over a list of changes in a chat](pictures/print-settings/revert-to-here.png)
- When a preset was saved from the chat, a line reading "Saved:" with the preset's name follows. Click **Undo** on that line to bring its earlier values back.
- To go back to an earlier state of the whole project, open the **File** menu and choose **Version history…**.

## Change printer or filament settings

These open a window with every setting of the printer or of a filament.

- Printer: click the printer's name in the header of the project, then **Printer settings…**. The **Printer** menu has the same item. With no printer chosen yet, it starts adding a printer.
- Filament: click the filament in the header of the project, then **Filament settings…**. With several filaments, pick one from the list first. The **Printer** menu has the same item for the first filament.

## Settings for one plate

1. In the **Plates** tab at the left, open the plate's "⋯" menu, or right-click the plate.
2. Choose **Plate settings…**.

![The Plates tab, with the ⋯ button at the right of a plate's row](pictures/print-settings/plates-tab.png)

The window holds what can differ per plate: the plate's name, its bed type, the print sequence, spiral vase, and the filament sequence of the first and the other layers. A setting made there shows in All settings with the note "Set on this plate".

## Settings for one object

An object can have settings of its own that differ from the project's. Its row in the **Plates** tab then carries a diamond mark, and the mark's menu says how many it has.

- To see them, open **All settings** and pick the object under **Showing**.
- To take one off, click **Use project value** on its row. A support blocker or enforcer has **Remove**.
- To add one or edit its value, ask AI in the chat, or use classic view.

![All settings showing one object, with Use project value beside its own Wall loops and Remove beside a support blocker](pictures/print-settings/object-settings.png)

## Classic view: every setting on screen

Classic view is the app's original screen, with all print settings in a panel at the side.

1. Open the **View** menu and choose **Switch to classic view…**. The "…" button in the header of the project has the same item.
2. A bar across the top says the window is in classic view. Click **Back to JusPrin** on it to return. The **View** menu also has **Switch to JusPrin view**.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on

RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on

target), or JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS. A run opens the app's window on this
computer's screen and takes real clicks: leave the screen unlocked and the
computer alone while it runs, about a minute a page. A run that fails is tried
once more before it counts. On a Mac grant Screen Recording to the program that starts this script (and to
the harness, if macOS asks), or the whole-window pictures come out black. A
black picture is refused, never copied. Pictures the app draws by itself, the
AI panel's and the plates panel's, need neither.
--keep DIR keeps every run's log and all the pictures it wrote. The pictures

"""
import argparse

import os

def harness():
    named = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named)
    built = [path for name in HARNESS_NAMES for path in (ROOT / "build").rglob(name) if path.is_file()]
    if not built:
        sys.exit("the shell harness is not built: build the shell_integration_harness target or set JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    return max(built, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)

    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point
    runner.CASES[GuideQuestion.name] = GuideQuestion
    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)

  - "Lock" or "Unlock"
  - "Plate settings…"
  - "Move to front" — only on plates after the first (OrcaOutline.cpp:264)
  - "Filament grouping" — only on a BBL printer with two extruders (OrcaOutline.cpp:267)

That menu is OrcaSlicer's stock menu, on every platform: Clone, Instances, Mirror, "Modify" (Split, Mesh boolean, Simplify, Fix), Delete, add part/modifier including "Text", Printable, per-object settings, and a "More" submenu (GUI_Factories.cpp:1745-1792, 1377-1437).

## 1. Steps and labels

**Where the menus are.** On Mac, File is in the menu bar (`Shell/AppMenus.cpp:127`). On Windows/Linux, File is a separate "File" button in the title bar (`AppMenus.cpp:131`, `BBLTopbar.cpp:292`). The File menu, in order, is `AppMenus.cpp:361-368`:
- "New project" (Ctrl+N), "Open…" (Ctrl+O), "Open recent"
- "Save" (Ctrl+S), "Version history…"
- "Import", "Export"
- then Quit. Windows calls it "Exit" (`:369-374`). The Mac also has "Preset Bundle" after Quit (`:366`).

OrcaSlicer's own Open Project, Recent files and Save Project are left out (`:322-325`). "Ctrl" means Cmd on Mac (`wxMOD_CMD`, `:238`). The window's key hook catches the shortcuts too (`:234-254`).

**The header's "…" button** (tooltip "Project details and preferences", `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:103`) opens, in order (`StatusRow.cpp:553-573`):
- the project name in bold, followed by its save state; it opens the Project tab
- "Version history"
- "Export project 3MF…"
- "Preferences…"
- "Switch to classic view…"

Two warning rows can appear under the name: "Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry." and "Some older project data couldn't be removed." (`:575-578`).

**Labels that differ by place:**

| Thing | File menu | Header menu / Project tab | Dialog |
|---|---|---|---|
| Versions | "Version history…" (`AppMenus.cpp:348`) | "Version history" (no ellipsis) | — |
| Export | File › Export › "Project 3MF…" (Ctrl+Shift+S, `:352`) | "Export project 3MF…" | title "Export project 3MF" |

**Steps:**

- **New project.** File › New project, or the Home button labelled just "New" (`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:219-224`). It saves the open project first and stays put if that save fails (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1371-1380`, `Shell/ShellController.cpp:565-574`).
- **Open….** File › Open… or Home's "Open…" (`App.tsx:225-230`). A file chosen in the dialog opens as a new project; Cancel leaves Home as it is (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1382-1393`).
- **Open recent.** A submenu of up to 10 saved projects, newest first. Unnamed ones show as "Untitled project". The item is greyed when there are none (`AppMenus.cpp:33, 516-540`).
- **Save.** Saves now and pins that version so it is kept and listed (`AppMenus.cpp:341-346`). It is disabled on Home.
- **Version history.** Switches to Prepare, opens the left pane and shows the Versions view (`ShellController.cpp:1568-1583`). Each row shows a local time and a "Restore" button. Only the button restores; clicking the time does nothing (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:580-624`). The current version is not listed. With nothing earlier, it says "No earlier saved versions yet." (`:588`).
- **Restore.** Opens a dialog titled "Restore project version" with buttons "Restore" / "Cancel". Its message: "Restore this version of the model and project settings? The current model will be saved as a version first. Conversations and print records will stay current." (`LeftPaneProject.cpp:169-176`). On failure: "Restore failed".
- **Export project 3MF.** A save dialog with default name "JusPrin project.3mf" and filter "3MF files (*.3mf)". On failure: "Export failed" / "The project couldn't be exported. Try again." (`LeftPaneProject.cpp:149-163`).
- **Project tab of the left pane.** The pane's tabs are "Plates" and "Project" (`Shell/LeftPane.cpp:876`). The root view (`LeftPaneProject.cpp:419-474`) shows:

  - a "MODEL" section: either "No title, designer or description yet." with a "+ Edit Project Info" button, or a cover picture, title, "by <designer>" and licence
  - rows "Print history", "Details", "Version history", "Export project 3MF…"
  
  Details has a back row, "Description", "Attachments" ("Bill of materials", "Assembly guide", "Others"), "Profile" and "Edit Project Info" (`:502-578`). Edit Project Info opens OrcaSlicer's own Project page editor (`ShellController.cpp:775-785`).
- **Project list on Home.**
  - Header: "Projects" with a count.
  - From 8 projects up: a "Search projects" box and a sort menu with "Recent" / "Name" (`App.tsx:24, 254-281`).
  - A "Drop a model or project here" tile (`:316-320`).
  - Each card shows a thumbnail, the name, a saved date ("Today", "Yesterday", "Oct 24"; `HomeUI/src/savedDate.ts`) and a status line ("Draft", "Printed …", "Sent …", "G-code exported …", "Printing on …"; `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:380-388, 973`). Clicking the card opens the project.
  - With no projects yet: "Drop a model or project to start" and "Your projects will appear here, most recent first." (`App.tsx:296-310`).
  - **There is no rename or delete for projects** anywhere: not in `ProjectCard.tsx`, the Home backend interface or the Home bridge protocol.

## 2. How it behaves

- **Where projects are stored:** `<data_dir>/jusprin/projects/<project-id>/` (`ShellController.cpp:438-442`).
- **When autosave saves.** A timer runs every 33 ms (`:715`). Autosave checks for changes every 2 s. It saves the model 1.5 s after the last edit, but not while a tool edit is in progress or an AI turn is running. Chat-only changes are written within 15 s at most (`Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:39-41, 632-684`).
- **Blank projects are never saved.** A project is saved once it holds a model, and stays saved after that (`ProjectAutosave.hpp:112-114`). An unnamed project takes its first object's file name (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:547-552`).
- **How many versions are kept:** up to 200 versions or 4 GB. Pinned versions are kept regardless: Save, Restore and AI before/after versions (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:42-43`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:943-992`).
- **What Restore does.** It saves the current state first, pins both versions, reloads the chosen model and settings, keeps the chats, and brings marked regions back with the model. It adds an undo boundary named "Restore project version" (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:1087-1152`).

- **A model dropped on the canvas** is added to the open project (`ShellController.cpp:262-290, 1074-1080`).
- **A .3mf opened anywhere** (including a drop on the canvas) opens as a project. If it was opened before, a "Previously opened file" dialog asks. Its buttons are "Continue current project", "Open existing project" or "Open most recent project", and "Create new project". If the file has changed since, "Create new project" becomes the default (`ShellController.cpp:575-650`).
- **After a restart** JusPrin starts on a blank project; nothing reopens on its own (`SH:3119-3130`).

<result>Every on-screen label below is copied from source. The Preferences page's labels are plain English strings in `Preferences.tsx`, not wrapped for translation. Paths below are relative to `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/hungry-murdock-3137cd/`, and `GUI/` means `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

## 1. Steps and labels

**Opening Preferences**
- **Mac:** app menu › "Preferences", **Cmd+,** (`src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.cpp:3620-3625`). The shortcut comes from `src/slic3r/GUI/Shortcuts.cpp:37`.
- **Windows/Linux:** title-bar menu › "Preferences" (`MainFrame.cpp:3639-3645`). OrcaSlicer's shortcut there is **Ctrl+P** (`Shortcuts.cpp:43`), and the shell adds **Ctrl+,** (`GUI/Shell/ShellController.cpp:1535-1541`).
- **Header "…" button** (tooltip "Project details and preferences", `GUI/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:103`) › "Preferences…", which shows ⌘, or Ctrl+, beside it (`StatusRow.cpp:52-58, 566`).
- **Home gear button**, tooltip "Preferences (Ctrl+,)". It says Ctrl+, on the Mac too, and the page also catches Ctrl/Cmd+, (`GUI/HomeUI/src/App.tsx:117-122, 245-246`).
- Every one of these opens JusPrin's window (`ShellController.cpp:917-928`). It is a modal titled "Preferences" (`GUI/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:151`) and opens on Account unless something asks for another section (`PreferencesWindow.cpp:195`).

**Sections** (`GUI/AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:36-43`): "Account", "BYOAI" (hint "Bring Your Own AI"), "Appearance", "3D view", "Projects & files", "Updates". Under the list is "More preferences…", which closes this window and opens OrcaSlicer's dialog (`:684-687`; `PreferencesWindow.cpp:336, 452-457`).

- **Appearance** (`:404-423`):
  - "Language": a searchable list.
  - "Theme": "Light" / "Dark".
  - "Units": "Millimetres" / "Inches".
- **3D view** (`:434-456`):
  - Group "Moving the view": "Controls" ("Mouse" / "Touchpad"), "Zoom toward the pointer", "Reverse scroll-wheel zoom", "Turn freely".
  - Group "Mouse buttons": "Left-drag", "Middle-drag", "Right-drag", each with "Turn the view" / "Pan" / "Nothing".
- **Projects & files** (`:465-485`):
  - "Version history" › "Show folder".
  - "Downloads" › "Save downloaded models to" with "Change…", which opens a dialog titled "Choose Download Directory" (`PreferencesWindow.cpp:314`).
  - "Open with JusPrin", tagged "Windows" and shown only there: "3MF projects", "STL and STEP models", "“Open in slicer” buttons on model sites".
- **Updates** (`:507-622`), the card states:
  - "Check now"
  - "Looking for a newer version on GitHub…" / "Checking…"
  - "Up to date · checked {ago}"
  - "Couldn’t reach GitHub" with "Try again"
  - "JusPrin {v} is available", with "Download" ("Opens the release page on GitHub"), "Skip this version", "Release notes" and "Full release notes on GitHub"
  - Microsoft Store builds: "Updates come from the Microsoft Store."
  - Group "What to check for": "New JusPrin versions" (a tick), and "Built-in printer and filament profiles".
  - When an update exists, the Updates entry in the list shows a dot labelled "Update available" (`:678-679`).

**View menu** (`GUI/Shell/AppMenus.cpp:377-418`), in order:
- "Home".
- **Mac:** "Show/Hide plates and project panel" and "Show/Hide AI panel"; the label changes. **Windows/Linux:** tick items "Plates and project panel" and "AI panel".
- OrcaSlicer's remaining View items, without "Show G-code Window" and "Reset Window Layout".
- "Switch to classic view…".
- When they are greyed out: the plates panel item works only on Prepare with no task open (`:395`). The AI panel item works only when a project is in front (`:402`).
- Header buttons do the same job:
  - "Show the Plates and Project panel" (`StatusRow.cpp:85`) and "Hide the Plates and Project panel" (`GUI/Shell/LeftPane.cpp:66`).
  - "Show the AI panel" / "Hide the AI panel" (`StatusRow.cpp:289`; `GUI/AgentUI/src/components/ChatNavigation.tsx:19-20`).
  - The capitalisation differs from the menu: "Project" in the tooltips, "project" in the menu.

**Classic view:** "Switch to classic view…" is in both the View menu and the header "…" menu (`StatusRow.cpp:567`). Going back is View › "Switch to JusPrin view" or the banner's "Back to JusPrin" (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:15439-15444`).

**Help menu** (`AppMenus.cpp:420-444`; `MainFrame.cpp:2909-2970`):
- JusPrin's items first: "JusPrin guide…", "Ask AI…", "Report a problem…".
- Then OrcaSlicer's: "Keyboard Shortcuts", "Show Configuration Folder", "Migrate Filament Presets", "Troubleshoot Center", "Open Network Test", "Benchmark 3D Scene", "Check for Updates", and "About JusPrin" (Windows/Linux only).
- "Setup Wizard" and "Show Tip of the Day" are removed.
- On the Mac, About is in the app menu (`AppMenus.cpp:140-144`).
- Keyboard Shortcuts is OrcaSlicer's own window; its key on the canvas is "?" (`Shortcuts.cpp:180`).

**Quit:**
- Mac: app menu, since the File menu's Quit is hidden (`AppMenus.cpp:363-367`).
- Windows: File › "Exit" (`:369-374`).
- Linux: File › "Quit", Ctrl+Q (`Shortcuts.cpp:181`).

**About window** (`GUI/Shell/AboutWindow.cpp`):
- Title "About JusPrin" (`:146`).
- "Version %s" and "Built on OrcaSlicer %s" (`:191-193`).
- "Build", plus "Copy version", which changes to "Copied" (`:197-206, 324`).
- "Get help": Email jusprin-support@obico.io, Discord, GitHub (`:235-243`).
- "License…" and "Free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3." (`:271-282`).

## 2. Behaviour facts

- **Language** is only stored; it takes effect when JusPrin restarts (`GUI/Preferences/PreferencesSettings.cpp:139-147`).
  - The page shows "JusPrin will use {X} after it restarts." with "Restart now" / "Later" (`Preferences.tsx:409-415`).
  - Restart saves the project, closes normally and relaunches (`PreferencesWindow.cpp:408-436`).
  - If the close is cancelled, nothing restarts and a message says so (`:432-434`).
- **Themes:** only Light and Dark, no "follow system" choice (`PreferencesSettings.cpp:108-115`). The change applies at once, 3D view included, with no restart (`PreferencesWindow.cpp:265-278`).
- **3D view settings** are saved immediately and shown by a redraw when the window closes (`ShellController.cpp:1500-1503`).
- **Update checks:**
  - JusPrin asks the GitHub releases API (`GUI/Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:20`).
  - The first check is about 10 s after start, then the timer runs hourly. A check happens only if 24 h have passed since the last attempt, or at startup if the last one failed (`UpdateCheck.cpp:21-23`; `GUI/Updates/UpdateRecord.cpp:67-73`).
  - It is skipped when "New JusPrin versions" is off or stealth mode is on (`UpdateCheck.cpp:79`). Automatic checks are on until turned off (`UpdateRecord.cpp:29`).
  - Pre-releases are offered only to test builds (`GUI/Updates/ReleaseFeed.cpp:16-23`).
  - **There is no in-app install.** "Download" opens the GitHub release page in the browser (`PreferencesWindow.cpp:330-333`).
  - Help › "Check for Updates" checks now and opens Preferences on Updates (`ShellController.cpp:2012-2020, 2084-2089`).
  - "Get the new version…" also brings back a version the person skipped (`:2091-2095`).
  - Built-in profiles are never fetched separately; they change only with a JusPrin release (`:2021-2026`).
- **Report a problem…** sends nothing by itself.
  - It opens the browser on `github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/issues/new`, pre-filled with "What happened: / What you expected: / Steps to make it happen again:" and a footer: "App version: JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer …)" and "System: <OS>" (`AppMenus.cpp:434-440`; `GUI/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:1030-1055`).
  - A body too long for the link is cut and ends "(Cut short to fit the link.)".
  - If the browser can't open: "The app couldn't open your browser." Inferred: submitting needs a GitHub account.

## 3. Test harness coverage

All checks print as `HARNESS CHECK <name> PASS|FAIL` (`shell_harness.cpp:8432-8437`).

**Default run, and inferred every non-stock shell mode** (through `verify_shell_installed`, `:1559, 8505`):
- Menu checks: `app_menus_help_menu` (only that "Report a problem…" is third and "Check for Updates" is present), `app_menus_view_menu`, `app_menus_title_bar_menu` (Windows/Linux, includes "Preferences"), `app_menus_view_greys_out_home_and_panels_on_home`, `app_menus_mac_panel_label_says_what_it_does` / `app_menus_panel_is_a_check_item`.
- They read labels only; none chooses a menu item.
- Panel toggling (`agent_pane_user_collapses_on_prepare`, `agent_pane_user_expands_on_prepare`) calls `toggle_agent_pane()` directly, not through the menu (`:8684-8693`).

<result>I've mapped the area from the code; the main findings are below. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` (`AgentUI/src/` shortened to `UI/`). Tests are in `tests/shell/`.

**Before writing, note these:**
- **The "Agent" section is labelled "BYOAI".** The Preferences sidebar shows **"BYOAI"** with the hint "Bring Your Own AI" (`UI/components/Preferences.tsx:38`).
- **Sign-in never happens in the AI panel.** The sign-in form is on the welcome screen, Home and Preferences › Account (`SignInDoor.tsx:1-6`). Every way to set up AI from the panel opens Preferences › Account, which is a modal window (`App.tsx:338`, `Shell/ShellController.cpp:1478-1491`).
- **The harness doc for `--live-agent-unavailable` is out of date.** It says the setup bar opens Preferences "on its Agent section". The check actually asserts it opens on `account`.

## 1. Steps and labels

**Chats list and New chat**
- In a chat, the header has **"Back to chats"** (chevron), **"New chat"** (+), **"Chat actions"** (⋯) and **"Hide the AI panel"** (`ChatNavigation.tsx:10, 324-333`). New chat is disabled while a reply is running.
- "Chat actions" offers **"Rename"**, which opens **"Rename chat"** with a **"Chat title"** field (1–120 characters), **"Cancel"** and **"Save"** (`:335-347`).
- It also offers **"Delete"**, which opens **"Delete chat?"**. The dialog says the project and its print history stay as they are. It can't delete a chat that is still working (`:349-352`).
- The list is titled **"Chats"**. When empty it says "No chats yet. Start a new chat about this project." Each row shows the title, a time ("Yesterday", "3 days ago", "Last week"…) and a preview line (`:384-395, 358-368`).
- The list footer button reads **"AI settings"**, or **"Set up AI"** when no AI is available. Either opens Preferences › Account (`:400-404`, `App.tsx:528`).

**Reopening an earlier chat**
- If the project still matches the chat's saved version, the chat simply becomes the current one. The project is not touched (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2238-2262`).
- Otherwise the chat opens read-only, with a notice in place of the message box (`App.tsx:423-457`):
  - Project changed: "The project has changed since this chat…" with **"Restore and resume"**. This asks **"Put the project back to <time>?"**, says "Your current version stays in Version history.", and offers **"Cancel"** / **"Restore and resume"** (`:767-777`).
  - Project unchanged: **"Resume saved setup"**.
  - Saved version missing: "JusPrin can't find the project version…". No resume button.
  - Always offered: **"Return to active chat"** and **"Ask current chat about this"**. The second puts a "From earlier chat …" quote into the current chat's message box.
- After a restore, the chat gets a note: "Restored this chat's saved project setup. Check the current printer and material before printing." (`AgentHost.cpp:2310`).

**Message box (composer)**
- **Model** picker: the menu groups models by provider. Above 12 models it gets a **"Search models"** field (`ModelPickers.tsx:25, 32, 122-124`).
- **Thinking** picker ("Thinking: <level>"), shown only if the model supports levels. Levels: Off, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, Extra high, Max, Fast, Thorough, or "Default" (`:19-23, 125-132`).
- Both pickers lock once you've sent a message. Hovering says: "A chat keeps the model and thinking level it started with. Start a new chat to change them." (`:134`).
- Account models show a price, e.g. "· 1 credit a message", plus what they're for (`ModelPickers.tsx:27-30`, `credits.ts:19-22`).
- Keys: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a new line (`Composer.tsx:231-237`). While a reply runs, Send becomes **"Stop"** (`:361-362`).
- Field placeholders: "Ask about this print or request a change…", "Reply…", "Or type your own answer…", "AI is responding…" (`:315-328`).

**Attachments**
- The + button (**"Attach a file"**) offers **"Photo or image"**, **"3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP)"**, **"G-code"** and **"Document (PDF)"**, using the system file dialog (`Composer.tsx:37-43, 348`).

- Each file shows as a row with **"Remove"**. If the model can't see pictures, the row says "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent." (`AttachmentChip.tsx:54, 65`).

**Reply choice chips**
- When the AI ends a reply with a "Choices: a | b" line, the options appear as buttons. Tapping one sends it as your message (`replyChoices.ts:1-40`, `MessageList.tsx:385-392`).
- Typing your own answer also works; the field then says "Or type your own answer…".

**Credits**
- A small ring next to the pickers (**"Credits left"**) opens a panel. It shows "N credits left", a bar per kind of credit (Sign-up / Free / <Plan> / Bought / Report credits) with expiry, and **"Get more credits"** / **"See usage"** (`BalancePanel.tsx:20-29, 91-114`).
- Preferences › Account shows the plan, **"Billing and usage"**, **"Get more credits"** and the credit bars (`Preferences.tsx:229-230`).
- These buttons open an in-app sheet titled "Credits and plans" or "Billing and usage", with **"Open in browser"** and **"Close"** (`Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:54, 289-295`).

**Signing in (Preferences › Account)**
- The account section is headed "JusPrin account" and shows the offer "Sign up and get 500 free credits" (`AgentConnection.tsx:114`, `credits.ts:41-53`).
- Google: **"Continue with Google"** → "Finish in your browser.", with **"Open the browser again"** and **"Use an email code instead"** (`SignInDoor.tsx:252-263, 292-294`).
- Email: type the address (placeholder "you@example.com"), then:
  - **"Sign up free"** sends a code straight away.
  - **"Sign in"** first asks how: **"Email me a 6-digit code"** or **"Use a password instead"** (`:301-307, 177-203`).
- Code screen: "Check your email.", 6 digit boxes, **"Send a new code"**, **"Change email"**, **"Sign in with Google instead"**, **"Cancel"** (`:132-159`).
- Signed in: "Signed in as …" with **"Sign out"**, and **"Delete account…"** (`AgentConnection.tsx:139, 194`; `Preferences.tsx:272`).

**Your own API key (Preferences › BYOAI)**
- Group "Your own API key": "Billed by your provider, not JusPrin. Stored on this computer only."
- Each provider row: **"Add key"** → paste the key → **"Check key"**. The row then shows "Key saved on this computer", with **"Replace"** / **"Remove"** (`AgentConnection.tsx:220, 283-326, 436`).
- **"New chats start with"** › Model sets the model for new chats (`Preferences.tsx:366-376`).

**Connecting an outside AI tool (MCP)**
- Group "Connect an AI tool you already use". Each tool says "Found on this computer" or "Not found on this computer" and has **"Connect…"**; there's also **"Look again"** (`AgentConnection.tsx:502-537`).
- Claude Code and Codex use a command: the screen shows it with **"Copy"**, **"Connect…"**, **"Close"** and an "Advanced / developer details" section (`SetupLocalTool.tsx:262-296`).
- The other tools show a review screen: "Allow this AI tool to read and change the open project?", what will change in the settings file, **"Connect"** / **"Cancel"** (`:301-331`).
- Then a progress screen ("Writing settings…"), then "Connected", "<tool> can see this project", and **"Done"** (`:217-258`).
- The tool list and commands, e.g. `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio jusprin -- …`, are in `Mcp/McpConnections.hpp:41-49`.

**Where Preferences is**
- **Mac:** app menu › "Preferences", ⌘, (`MainFrame.cpp:3620-3625`, `Shortcuts.cpp:37`).
- **Windows/Linux:** "Preferences" in the menu inside the title bar, Ctrl+P (`MainFrame.cpp:3639-3646`, `Shortcuts.cpp:43`). JusPrin adds Ctrl+, (`ShellController.cpp:1535-1541`).
- **All platforms:** the project header's overflow menu has **"Preferences…"**, labelled ⌘, or Ctrl+, (`StatusRow.cpp:52-58, 566`).

**When AI isn't set up**
- Header: "AI" with a "NOT SET UP" badge.
- Empty chat: "No AI connected", a **"Set up AI"** button, and "Registered JusPrin account, your own key, or an AI tool you already use." (`Panels.tsx:67-90`).
- Once the chat has content: a bar with **"Set up AI"** and "Chatting here needs AI." (`:120-123`).

## 2. Facts people will ask about
- **Providers for your own key:** Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter (`AgentConnection.tsx:23-27`).
- **Chats are per project.** They're stored in the project's own document (`AgentHost.cpp:32-45`); the list is labelled "Project chats".

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 11 13:41:13 2026 -0800

    Help › JusPrin guide…: a window that searches the app guide and shows its pages
    
    The Help menu gains "JusPrin guide…" above Ask AI…. It opens a window over
    the app, not modal, 960 × 680: the guide's pages at the left in the order
    docs/guide/README.md lists them, the open page's sections under its title,
    and the page itself at the right with its pictures. Typing in "Search the
    guide" narrows the left to the sections that hold every typed word, with the
    words marked; picking one opens its page at that section. Escape empties the
    search. Choosing the menu item again brings the open window to the front.
    The design is on the canvas "JusPrin v2", page "JusPrin guide window", and is
    a proposal Kenneth has not approved.
    
    How it is built:
    - The window is the Agent page in a new mode, ?panel=guide
      (AgentPageMode::Guide, Shell/GuideWindow), as Preferences and the import
      windows are. The page carries every docs/guide page and picture, packed in
      when it is built (guidePages.ts), so nothing is installed beside it. That
      took the page from 795 KB to 1.29 MB; WebKit on a Mac opened it in 24 ms
      instead of 22. Web/CMakeLists.txt rebuilds the page when docs/guide changes.
    - The page drops what only AI reads (the ai-description line and ai: notes)
      and opens a link out of the guide in the browser only when it is https.
    - Pictures are taken at twice the screen's size and shown at half, so they
      match the app. plates-tab.png was the one taken at screen size; it is
      doubled, and guide_checks.json's "atScreenSize" makes run_guide_checks.py
      double it on the next run.
    - Sizes are tokens (component.guide in design-tokens.json, with a guard in
      test_brand_tokens.cpp).
    
    Web view windows share two pieces of code that six of them each carried:
    
    - Waiting before a web view is destroyed. On macOS a window closed right
      after it opens crashes the app if its web view goes while WebKit is still
      installing the page's script handler. The guide window hit this first.
      Agent/WebViewRelease now does the waiting: request() runs the release step
      now, or retries every 50 ms while an install is running, and cancel()
      drops it. Home's printer pop-out, the credits sheet, the Add a printer

    1. tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py runs the shell harness modes that
       guide_checks.json names for each page, in the app as built. A run with
       "checks" is judged by those named checks alone and stopped once they pass,
       so a failure elsewhere in a mode is reported apart and does not block the
       page. A failed run is tried once more, because a run takes real clicks and
       loses them when another window comes to the front. The pictures a page
       uses are cropped from the run's own and copied to
       docs/guide/pictures/<page>/; a blank one is refused.
    2. guide.test.ts rebuilds each page's skill and now also fails when a section
       has no harness run, when a picture is not one a run took or is missing,
       and when a page has fewer than three questions.
    3. With --ask-ai, tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py asks the model the
       questions in guide_questions.json and has a judge read the replies;
       --no-guide runs them with the guides off the list.
    
    The print settings page gains five pictures taken this way, and its step
    about Revert to here now says it is the arrow button beside a change, which
    the picture showed.

<result>Several things in the code differ from what the brief assumed. Nothing here was run, so every pass/fail statement comes from reading the code. Paths below are relative to `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/hungry-murdock-3137cd/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, and the harness is `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`.

- **"Set it up myself" is not an on-screen label.** It only appears in harness comments. The Add a printer chat's header link reads **"Browse the full printer list"**, or **"Open printer settings"** when the chat is about one printer (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx:602-603`). That link opens JusPrin's own add-printer form. OrcaSlicer's printer wizard runs only from the fallback shown when the chat page fails to load (`PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp:108-112`, `PrinterConversation.cpp:1251-1262`).
- **The project header has no Connect….** The code comment says Connect… was deferred (`Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:142-146`). Connect… exists only on Home.

## 1. Steps and labels

**Printer and filament chip (Prepare header).** The chip is hidden on Home (check `header_hidden_on_home`).
- The printer half shows "Select printer" when no printer is set. Otherwise it shows "name · nozzle", plus a warning icon and "from the file" when the printer came inside a project file (`PrinterFilamentChip.cpp:55-65`). The filament half shows "Select filament" when empty (`:78`). Left and right arrow keys move between the two halves (`:37-48`).
- **Printer menu**, top to bottom (`Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`):
  - The printer's name, or "No printer selected", with a status word: Ready, Printing, Paused, Connected, Offline, "Checking connection…" or "Not connected". "Not connected" adds "Export the G-code to print from a card." A printer from a file shows "From the file · not one of your printers" (`:95-147`). Clicking the row opens the printer window (`:149-161`).
  - "Nozzle": read-only (`:169-171`).
  - "Plate" › a sub-list of plate types with a tick on the current one (`:175-183`, `:267-278`).
  - "OTHER PRINTERS": click one to switch the project's printer (`:197-208`).
  - "Printer settings…" (`:222`), "Ask AI about printer settings…" (`:234`), "Calibrate…" (`:244`), "Add a printer…" (`:257`).
- **Filament menu** (`Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp`):
  - "Use what's loaded on the printer…" appears only when the printer reports trays. When it is offline the row is greyed with "%s is offline. Turn it on to read what's loaded." (`:340-346`).
  - Title "FILAMENT FOR %s", or "FILAMENTS FOR %s" with numbered slot rows when there is more than one slot (`:369`, `:426`).
  - "COLOUR" swatch row; the last swatch's tooltip is "Other colour…" and opens the system colour picker (`:162-176`, `:546-564`).
  - "FILAMENTS FOR THIS PRINTER" list (`:435`), "Other filament…" (`:458`), "Filament settings…" (`:472`), "Ask AI about filament settings…" (`:477`), "Calibrate this filament…" (`:487`).
  - "Add another filament to this print" (`:392`, `:499`). It is not offered inside a slot's own view (`:497`).

**Printer menu in the menu bar** (`Shell/AppMenus.cpp:488-512`): "Add a printer…", "Printer settings…", "Ask AI about printer settings…", "Filament settings…", "Ask AI about filament settings…", "Calibrate…".
- On Mac it is a menu-bar menu placed right after Print, which follows View (`:159-164`).
- On Windows/Linux it is a submenu of the menu inside the title bar, also after View and Print (`:165-174`).
- It works over any screen, Home included (`:484-485`).

**Home printer card** (`HomeUI/src/components/PrinterMenu.tsx`):
- The kebab button has the tooltip "Printer actions" (`:136`). Its items: "Connect…" (saved printers only), "Printer settings…", "Ask AI about printer settings…", "Calibrate…" (saved printers only), "Rename", "Remove printer…" (`:145-188`).
- Rename opens a "Rename printer" dialog with a "Printer name" field and Cancel / Save (`:221-248`).
- Remove asks "Remove printer?" with the text "Remove “X”? Its printer settings will be deleted. Your projects stay." and Cancel / Remove (`:253-268`).
- Bambu cloud devices use OrcaSlicer's own rename and unbind dialogs instead (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1606-1634`).
- The card also has an "Open printer window" button, "Connect…" or "Reconnect", and the note "Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin" (`PrinterCard.tsx:256-267`).

**Adding a printer on Home.** "+ Add printer" (`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:356-357`), or "Add your printer" on the "No printer yet" card (`PrinterCard.tsx:76-79`), opens the chat titled "Add a printer". For Connect it is titled "Connect X", and for settings "X settings" (`ChatNavigation.tsx:293-297`).
- The form steps are "Which printer?" (Brand / Model; Cancel / Next), "Which plate is on it?" and a filament step ending in "Skip — start with X" (`AddPrinterForm.tsx:101-124`, `:262`).
- Closing asks "Close this chat?" with "Close chat" (`App.tsx:616-621`).
- Connecting shows a form with "Access code" (Bambu) or "API key", the note "Stays on this computer.", and Connect / "Help me find the code" (or "…key") / Cancel (`PrinterPanel.tsx:196-212`).

**Importing printers.**
- File › Import › "Import from OrcaSlicer..." and "Import from JusPrin 1...". These use three ASCII dots, not "…" (`src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.cpp:3137-3143`; `dots` is defined at `GUI_App.hpp:183`).
- The import window is titled "Import from %s", then "Imported from %s" (`Home/OrcaImportWindow.cpp:44`, `:165`).
- In first launch: "Import from JusPrin 1…" / "Import from OrcaSlicer…", leading to "Bring your printers from X?" with Import and Skip for now (`Onboarding.tsx:229`, `:275-295`).

**Calibrate…** (`Shell/ShellController.cpp:1352-1366`). It shows a "Calibrate %s?" dialog with Start, or "Set up AI…" when no AI is set up, plus Cancel. The dialog says the open project will be saved and closed, and that the test's settings are temporary.

## 2. Behaviour facts

- **No printer chosen:** "Printer settings…" opens the Add a printer chat, and "Calibrate…" is disabled (`PrinterMenu.cpp:219-245`; `AppMenus.cpp:492-512`).
- **Skipping first launch** sets up a stand-in "Generic printer" (Generic Klipper, 0.4 mm nozzle) (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:920-922`). Home then explains: "Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer…" (`Onboarding.tsx:27`).
- **Connection types:** Bambu Lab over LAN or Cloud (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:244`), Moonraker and OctoPrint (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:825-850`). Any other type gets "…which this chat does not connect…" (`:587-588`). Bambu printers need Bambu's network plug-in ("Bambu plug-in needed", `PrinterPanel.tsx:109`).
- **Removing a printer:** projects stay. It is refused if other printer profiles are based on this one (`Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp:251-253`). Removing a custom printer also deletes its filament and process profiles, through OrcaSlicer's confirm (`:256-268`). Removing the selected printer selects its parent profile (`:270-278`).
- **Rename rules:** the name cannot be empty, cannot contain `< > [ ] : / \ | ? * "`, cannot differ from the old one only in capitalisation, and cannot match another printer's name (`PrinterMenu.tsx:21-29`).
- **Import:** copies printers with their filaments and print settings; the other app keeps its own copy (`Onboarding.tsx:277`). Sources are the OrcaSlicer data folder or JusPrin 1's "JusPrin" folder (`Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:129-134`). JusPrin 1 also brings Bambu's network file; its own app settings and sign-in never come along (`V1Import/V1Import.hpp:5-23`).

## 3. Harness coverage

Each check prints `HARNESS CHECK <name> PASS|FAIL` (`check()` at `shell_harness.cpp:8432`).

- **Default mode (no flag)** (`:8929-8939`):
  - Chip arrow keys: `right_arrow_moves_to_the_filament_half`.
  - Plate sub-list: `plate_substep_keeps_the_menu_open_after_a_click`, `nozzle_row_is_read_only`. No plate type is actually picked.
  - Filament and colour: `the_project_is_on_the_picked_filament`, `a_colour_click_sets_the_slot_colour`.
  - Adding a filament: `adding_a_slot_adds_one`.
  - Menu bar: `app_menus_printer_menu`, `app_menus_print_and_printer_follow_view` (Mac), `app_menus_title_bar_menu` (Windows/Linux) (`:8579-8605`).
  - Chip pictures `light.png`, `dark.png`, `long-name.png`, drawn by the app itself, written to `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR` (otherwise a temporary folder that is deleted) (`:9130-9160`).
- **--printer-menu:** switching printer: `printer_menu_switches_the_projects_printer`, `printer_menu_switch_refreshes_the_chip`; from-file printer: `file_printer_is_marked_from_the_file`.
- **--printer-menu-capture:** the same checks plus `printer-menu-other-printers.png`, which is a screen grab (`blit_screen`), so it will come out black.
- **--task-chat:** Printer settings… and Ask AI: `header_printer_settings_opens_the_window`, `header_printer_settings_is_about_the_selected_printer`, `header_printer_manual_settings_open`. Home routes: `home_add_opens_task_chat`, `home_settings_covers_home_with_correct_context`, `home_connect_opens_task_chat`. These go through backend calls, not clicks on the cards.
- **--printer-setup:** add chat `panel_opens_from_add_printer`; form via messages `form_saves_the_printer_under_its_own_name`, `form_starts_the_printer_on_the_chosen_plate`; no-AI path `printer_offer_opens_preferences`.
  - Rename and remove are tested through the printer-store functions, not the Home dialogs: `named_rename_of_the_selected_printer`, `named_rename_refuses_illegal_characters`, `named_remove_of_the_selected_printer_selects_its_parent`.
  - The known failure, `selection_interruption_does_not_blame_credentials`, is in `verify_saved_bambu_connection` (`:7079`), so treat that function's checks with care.
- **--calibration-capture:** `calibration_filament_menu_has_the_row`, `calibration_home_dialog_names_the_printer_and_no_filament`, `calibration_row_follows_printer_settings`, `calibration_popup_names_the_filament_and_printer`, `calibration_project_asks_which_test`.
  - Web view snapshots (real pictures): `0-symptom-chat`, `2-dialog-from-filament-cancelled`, `3-home-card-menu`, `4-dialog-from-home-cancelled`, `6-dialog-from-printer-started`, `7-chat-asks-which-test`, `8-test-project-chat`, `9-reading-the-tower`, `10-saved`, `11-reopened`, `12-undone`, `13-home`.
  - Screen grabs (black): `1-filament-menu`, `5-printer-menu`, `7-window` through `11-window`.
- **--home-live:** checks `home_live_connect_starts`, `the_tray_row_leads_and_is_live`, `an_offline_printer_keeps_the_tray_row_greyed`.
  - It is probably broken (inferred). Its card reader looks for `.printer-fact dd` and a "Launch monitor" button (`:8141-8144`, `:8255`). The card actually renders `.printer-facts` and "Open printer window", and never shows "Online". So `home_live_page_shows_online` likely times out.
- **--fresh-example:** `choose_my_printer_shows_the_add_printer_form`, `default_printer_marked_assumed`. These use backend calls, not page clicks.
- **No mode walks:**
  - choosing a plate type;
  - "Add a printer…" from the menus;
  - the card kebab's Rename, Remove, Connect… and Printer settings… clicked on the page;
  - the Rename and Remove dialogs (only HomeUI unit tests, `PrinterCard.test.tsx`);
  - File › Import from OrcaSlicer / JusPrin 1 and the first-launch import screens;
  - "Other filament…" and "Use what's loaded on the printer…" from a project;
  - OrcaSlicer's wizard itself (`:6886-6889` says it cannot be driven).

## 4. Boundary

The calibration flow after Start (the test project, reading the tower, saving) and the AI connect chat behave like their own areas. This page could end at the Calibrate… dialog and at "Connect…", and link out from there. First-launch import belongs with onboarding; File › Import is the part that belongs on this page.</result>

<!-- ai-description: Read before telling the person how to start, open, save, find or export a project by hand: New, Open…, Open recent, dropping a file, autosave and Save, Version history and Restore, Export project 3MF, the Project tab, and the project list on Home. -->

# Projects and files

How JusPrin keeps your work, and how to open, save and export it.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux the **File** menu is the **File** button in the title bar, and the other menus are in the menu beside it.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can open a file the person attached for them; I cannot save, restore or export a project myself, so for those I give these steps. -->

## Start a project or open a file

Every project is kept by JusPrin itself, in its own folder of projects. A file you open is copied into a new project; the file itself is left as it was.

- **New project** in the **File** menu, or **New** on Home, starts an empty project. The project you were in is saved first.
- **Open…** in the **File** menu, or **Open…** on Home, opens a model or a project file as a new project. The files it opens are STL, 3MF, STEP, OBJ, AMF, SVG and ZIP.
- Dropping a file on Home, or opening one from Finder or Explorer, also opens it as a new project.
- Dropping a model on the 3D view of an open project adds it to that project. A 3MF file opens as a project of its own wherever it is dropped.
- **Open recent** in the **File** menu lists the last ten projects, newest first. It is greyed out while there are none.

The shortcuts are Cmd+N and Cmd+O on a Mac, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+O on Windows and Linux.

## Open a file you opened before

When you open a 3MF file that is already one of your projects, JusPrin asks what to do before it opens anything:

- **Continue current project** keeps working in the project that is open.
- **Open existing project** (or **Open most recent project**, when the file made more than one) goes to the project you made from it before.
- **Create new project** opens the file again as a separate project. When the file has changed since you last opened it, this is the button already chosen.

![The question asked when a 3MF file that is already a project is opened again](pictures/projects-and-files/reopen-question.png)

## Saving

JusPrin saves the project by itself: a moment after you stop changing it, and never while AI is in the middle of a change. The project's name in the header of the project is followed by **Saving…**, **Saved** or **Couldn't save**.

- **Save** in the **File** menu (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) saves now and keeps that version for good, so it stays in Version history.
- An empty project is never saved. It is saved once it holds a model, and from then on even if you empty it.
- A project without a name takes the name of the first model in it.
- If saving fails, for example because the disk is full, the "…" menu at the right of the header says **Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.**, and saving starts again by itself once it can.

## Go back to an earlier version

Each save is kept as a version. JusPrin keeps up to 200 of them, and always keeps the ones you saved with Save and the ones from before and after a change AI made.

1. Choose **Version history…** in the **File** menu, or **Version history** in the "…" menu at the right of the header. The panel at the left opens on the project's versions, newest first.
2. Click **Restore** beside the version you want. Clicking the time does nothing.
3. Click **Restore** in the question that opens.

![The project's versions in the panel at the left, each with a Restore button](pictures/projects-and-files/version-history.png)

The model and the project's settings go back to that version. What you had is saved as a version first, so you can go back to it the same way. Chats and print records stay as they are.

To take back one change AI made in a chat, use **Revert to here** beside the change instead; the guide's page on print settings describes it.

## Export the project as a 3MF file

Projects stay in JusPrin's own folder. To give a project to someone, or to open it in another program, export it:

1. Choose **Export project 3MF…** in the "…" menu at the right of the header, or in the File menu choose **Export**, then **Project 3MF…** (Cmd+Shift+S on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux).
2. Pick where to save it. It is saved first, then written there.

The 3MF file holds the model, the plates and the settings. It does not hold the chats.

## The Project tab

The panel at the left of the 3D view has two tabs, **Plates** and **Project**. It starts hidden: click the button at the left of the header, or choose **Plates and project panel** in the **View** menu, to show it. Then click **Project**.

![The Project tab, with the project's name, its model information and the Print history, Details, Version history and Export project 3MF… rows](pictures/projects-and-files/project-tab.png)

- The top shows the project's name and whether it is saved.
- **MODEL** shows the model's title, designer and picture, when the file brought them. Otherwise it says **No title, designer or description yet.** with **+ Edit Project Info** to add them.
- **Print history**, **Details**, **Version history** and **Export project 3MF…** open those. Details holds the description, the attached files and the designer's profile.

## Your projects on Home

Home lists every project under **Projects**, most recent first, each with a picture of its plate, its name, when it was saved and what happened to it last, such as printed or exported. Click a project to open it.

To get to Home from a project, click the house button at the left of the header, or choose **Home** in the **View** menu.

![Home, with a project in the Projects list beside the tile for dropping a file](pictures/projects-and-files/home-projects.png)

- With eight projects or more, **Search projects** and a choice between **Recent** and **Name** appear above the list.
- Dropping a file anywhere on Home opens it as a new project.
- A project cannot be renamed or deleted from Home.

When you open a 3MF file that is already one of your projects, JusPrin asks what to do before it opens anything:

- **Open existing project** (or **Open most recent project**, when the file made more than one) goes to the project you made from it before.
- **Create new project** opens the file again as a separate project. When the file has changed since you last opened it, this is the button already chosen.

## Saving

JusPrin saves the project by itself: a moment after you stop changing it, and never while AI is in the middle of a change. The project's name in the header of the project is followed by **Saving…**, **Saved** or **Couldn't save**.

- **Save** in the **File** menu (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) saves now and keeps that version for good, so it stays in Version history.
- An empty project is never saved. It is saved once it holds a model, and from then on even if you empty it.
- A project without a name takes the name of the first model in it.

3. Click **Restore** in the question that opens.

2. Pick where to save it. It is saved first, then written there.

- With eight projects or more, **Search projects** and a choice between **Recent** and **Name** appear above the list.
- Dropping a file anywhere on Home opens it as a new project.
- A project cannot be renamed or deleted from Home.

<!-- ai-description: Read before telling the person how to arrange things by hand on the plates: the Plates tab and its plate and object menus (Arrange, Auto-orient, Split, Fix model, number of instances), Add model, Add plate, the Move, Rotate and Scale tools on the 3D view, More, and cut or paint keys. -->

# Plates and objects

How to put models on plates and move, turn, size, copy and split them by hand.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are in the menu beside the **File** button in the title bar.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can import, place, lay out, repair and split objects myself with my tools when the person asks me to; I give these steps when they want to do it themselves or ask where something is. -->

## The Plates tab

The panel at the left of the 3D view lists the project's plates and what is on each. It starts hidden. To show it, click the button at the far left of the header (**Show the Plates and Project panel**), or choose **Show plates and project panel** in the **View** menu (on Windows and Linux, tick **Plates and project panel**). The panel has two tabs; **Plates** is the first.

![The Plates tab with two plates, the first open with its object, and the Add model and Add plate buttons under the list](pictures/plates-and-objects/plates-tab.png)

- Each plate's row says whether it is sliced: **Sliced**, **Not sliced yet** or **Slicing…**.
- Click a plate to make it the plate you are working on. Only that plate is open in the list; a closed plate shows a short summary such as its object's name or how many objects it holds.
- Click an object to select it in the 3D view. Selecting an object in the 3D view selects it here too.
- A row may carry **Mesh needs repair**, **won't print**, the number of its filament, or "×2" and more for copies.
- A diamond mark on a row means the plate or object has settings or painting of its own. Click it to see which.

## A plate's menu

Point at a plate's row and click the "⋯" button at its right, or right-click the row. The menu has:

- **Rename** to name the plate.
- **Arrange** to lay out the objects on this plate only.
- **Auto-orient** to turn this plate's objects to the side that prints best.
- **Lock** to keep Arrange from moving this plate's objects. **Unlock** undoes it.
- **Plate settings…** for what can differ per plate, such as its bed type. The guide's page on print settings describes the window.
- **Move to front**, on plates after the first, to make it plate 1.
- **Delete plate**, when the plate can be deleted.

## An object's menu

Point at an object's row and click "⋯", or right-click the row:

- **Rename** to name the object.
- **Set number of instances…** to print several copies of it. Each copy then has a row of its own, with **Delete copy** in its menu.
- **Printable** to leave the object on the plate without printing it. Its row then says **won't print**.
- **Change filament**, when the print uses more than one filament, to print the object in another one.
- **Fix model**, when the model's mesh has errors, to repair it.
- **Split**, then **To objects** to make each separate piece its own object, or **To parts** to keep the pieces as parts of one object.
- **Delete** to take the object off the plate.

![An object's menu in the Plates tab, with Rename, Set number of instances…, Printable, Split and Delete](pictures/plates-and-objects/object-menu.png)

## Add a model or a plate

Under the list in the Plates tab:

- **Add model** opens a file and adds it to the plate you are working on. Dropping a model on the 3D view does the same.
- **Add plate** adds an empty plate after the last one. It is greyed out when no more plates fit.

With nothing in the project, the 3D view says **Drop a model here or add one**.

## Move, rotate and scale an object

Select an object, and a row of buttons appears at the top left of the 3D view: Move, Rotate, Scale, a button that adds a copy, and **More**. The keys M, R and S open the first three as well.

![The Rotate tool open under the row of buttons, with the angle typed in](pictures/plates-and-objects/rotate-tool.png)

- **Move**: drag the arrows in the 3D view, or type a position under **Position**. **World coordinates** or **Object coordinates** chooses which way the axes point.
- **Rotate**: type an angle under **Rotate (relative)** to turn the object by it, or under **Rotate (absolute)** to set its angle. Press Return to apply what you typed. A reset button beside a row puts the angle back to where it was when the tool opened.
- **Scale**: type a percentage under **Scale** or a size in mm under **Size**. **Uniform scale** keeps the proportions.
- Click the tool's button again, or **Done**, to close it.
- The copy button (**Add instance**) adds one copy of the selected object. Undo takes it away again.

## More: mirror, text and other tools

**More**, the last button in the row, opens the object menu of the 3D view, the same one a right-click on an object opens. It has **Clone**, **Mirror**, the parts and modifiers you can add, including **Text**, and the object's other commands.

Cutting and painting have no button. With an object selected, press a key in the 3D view:

- C to cut the object in two.
- L to paint where supports go, P to paint where seams go, N to paint colours on a multi-material print, H to paint fuzzy skin.
- F to lay a chosen face flat on the plate.
- T to add text on the object.

Each tool shows its own controls on the 3D view. Press Escape, or the same key, to close it.
